sentences.text: 1. Petitioner who is widow of late Manthirram who succumbed to the injuries in the police station and died during the course of treatment has filed this writ petition seeking following relief(s) :-

"I. The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to issue the writ in the nature of mandamus by directing that entire matter be investigated by the respondent No.2 i.e.
C.B.I. II.

The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondent No.1 to pay Rs.20,00,000/-
 to the dependents of the deceased as  compensation.
III. The Hon'ble Court be please to direct the respondent No.1 to punish the responsible police officer (respondent No.5 to 11) and registered the criminal case against the respondents.
IV. The Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to call the entire record of the petitioner's case.

Any other relief which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.
VI. The cost of petition may kindly also be awarded in favour of petitioners."

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this writ petition are that on 26.05.2006 at about 10.30 AM, quarrel took place between Manthirram, his children Harish Verma and Ku. Neelam Verma with Pitamber Verma and his wife.

Pitamber Verma lodged report to the concerned police station on the same day at about 1.30 PM and based on the report, Crime No.132/06 for alleged commission of offence under Section 294, 323, 506, 341 and 34 of I.P.C. was registered against Mantirram Verma, Harish Verma and Ku. Neelam Verma.

According to the pleading made in the writ petition Manthirram Verma along with his children also went to concerned police station for lodging of report as they also suffered injuries in the quarrel, however, police hold up Manthirram Verma in the police station and left his children to go.

In the evening Manthirram Verma had a talk with his wife through phone and on next day morning she received phone call from the police station stating that her husband is admitted in District Hospital.
She rushed to the hospital where she found that police officials are making arrangement to shift her husband from District Hospital to Sector-9 Hospital, Bhilai.
She was also asked to go along with injured Manthirram Verma, however, during course of treatment, he died in Sector-9 Hospital, Bhilai.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that on 26.05.2006 respondent No.12 abused in filthy language to children of petitioner namely Harish Verma aged about 16 years and daughter Neelam aged about 14 years assaulted them and threatened to kill them.
Husband of petitioner along with his children went to lodge the report to the concerned police station, borrowing motor cycle of Sitaram (brother of Manthirram Verma).

Oral report of Manthirram Verma was not accepted and he was asked to bring written report which was also prepared and he again came to police station along with written report, however, Manthirram Verma was taken into custody and children were sent to home.

At the time when Manthirram Verma was taken into custody, he was in good health conditions, he also talked to his wife near about 7 to 7.30 PM and intimated her that he was taken into custody and asked her to make arrangement for his release on bail tomorrow.

In the same evening on 26.05.2006 at about 9.00 PM when son of Manthirram Verma gave telephone call to concerned police station and requested police officials that he wanted to talk to Manthirram Verma to which police officials present in the police station stated that he may talk to his father next morning.

In the next morning, police gave phone call in the house of Chain Singh (Baba) of village Suvatala where petitioner was called and intimated that her husband is hospitalized at District Hospital, Rajnandgaon.

Petitioner immediately rushed to hospital along with Sitaram and Anusuiya Bai and saw that, her husband Manthirram Verma was in unconscious condition, injuries over the head face and his toe and some sign of electric current shock was also appearing.
Husband of petitioner was referred to Sector-9 Hospital, Bhilai on 27.05.2006.
While his treatment in Sector-9 Hospital at Bhilai deceased gain consciousness and had stated that police gave beating and again became unconscious.
Later on succumbed to the injuries.
Late Manthirram Verma died due to injuries caused by the police officials in Police Station - Dongargarh, District - Rajnandgaon.
In postmortem report, it is mentioned that injuries suffered by late Manthirram Verma was antemortem in nature and there was abrasion over the body.

Injuries have been caused by hard and Smt. Indrabai vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37199428/

Police of Police Station - Dongargarh had prepared concocted story that at the time of lodging report, Manthirram Verma became unconscious and suddenly fell down due to which he suffered injuries.
The death of petitioner was due to custodial torture and assault, in violation of human dignity.

Late Manthirram Verma was working as Supervisor at Bajrang Power Ispat Limited and earning Rs.5,000/- per month and petitioner has no other source of income, therefore, petitioner be awarded suitable amount of compensation and further a direction be issued to Central Bureau of Investigation for proper investigation into the matter.
The police personnel failed to give plausible explanation as to how Manthirram Verma suffered injuries when his children left Manthirram Verma in the evening in a good health condition.
Custodial death is one of the worst crime and is protected under Article 21 and 22 (1) of the Constitution of India.
He contended that as the incident is of police station, the report submitted by Sub-Divisional Magistrate also does not mention the correct conclusion.
From the report submitted it is clearly depicting that report is not prepared in fair manner.
Petitioner be awarded compensation, the respondent/CBI be directed to investigate the incident of death of late Manthirram Verma.
4. Learned counsel for State opposes the submission of learned counsel for petitioner and would submit that deceased lodged report in the concerned police station at about 12.20 hours.

They were sent for their medical examination and when upon examining it reveal that no cognizable offence is made out against Pitambar, proceedings under Section 155 of Cr.P.C. was initiated on his complaint.
Thereafter, Pitambar lodged report at about 13.30 hours.
Pitambar and his injured wife were also sent for medical examination and based on their medical report, crime was registered bearing No.132 of 2006.

Deceased again came to the police station at about 20.35 hours with written report,
where upon Crime No.136 of 2006 for offence under Section 294, 506B, 323/34 of I.P.C. and Section 5 of Tonhi Pratadna Adhiniyam was registered.
When Manthirram Verma came to police station second time in the night, he suddenly fell down at the time of lodging report.
Thereafter, it was noticed that he suffered paralysis attack on his left side of his body, Rojnamchasanha was prepared and he was taken to hospital where he remained from 26.05.2006 to 31.05.2006.
Death was not during custody but deceased died during the treatment in hospital.
In the police station late Manthirram Verma has not suffered any injuries, it appears that in the hospital he suffered some injuries as he fell down from bed and succumbed to the head injuries.
During treatment, deceased was also sent for CT scan of his head, from which it is clearly reflecting that deceased did not suffer any head injury.
Respondents made query with concerned doctor whether the injuries suffered by deceased could be caused as a result of felling, doctor opined in affirmative.

Death of late Manthirram Verma is not due to any police atrocity but due to paralysis attack, treatment of which was being given by doctors at District Hospital, Rajnandgaon as also the doctors of Sector-9 Hospital, Bhilai.

Magisterial enquiry was directed and during the Magisterial Enquiry, statements of doctors were also recorded, from which it is clearly reflecting that deceased suffered head injuries due to his felling on ground in police station of his own.
He suffered paralysis attack of his left part of the body and further he also fell down from bed in the hospital during treatment.

After death,
villagers agitated upon which second time postmortem of dead body of deceased Manthirram Verma was again conducted.
During the Magisterial Enquiry, none of doctors who examined the deceased stated about any serious injuries.
No sign of cruelty/torture or assault is reported or opined.
Death of deceased is natural.

Mr. B.P. Singh, learned counsel for respondents No.5 to 11 submits that petitioner when came to lodged report in the police station second time along with written report, after getting the report registered he immediately fell down.
Police Officials present there noted that one part of body of petitioner suffered paralysis attack.

During course of examination in the hospital, deceased again fell down from bed, which was taken note of, by Sub-Divisional Magistrate in its enquiry report based on the statement of Dr. Suchita Shrivastava, Medical Officer, Community Health Centre,
Dongargarh.
Second postmortem which was conducted by three doctors under pressure due to agitation opined no new injuries, FSL is also negative.
During enquiry, petitioner was also called and her statement was recorded.
No opinion is given of cause of death in second postmortem report.

6. Mr. Vibhav Goverdhan, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.2/CBI submits that it is not a case which requires investigation from CBI, however, if Court comes to the conclusion that enquiry by the respondent CBI is necessary, and directs, then appropriate steps will be taken in this regard complying the order passed by this Court.
7. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.13 and 14 supports the submission made by learned State counsel.

8. Mr. Kotecha, learned counsel for petitioner in reply to the submission made by learned counsel for respective respondents would submit that enquiry conducted by Sub- Divisional Magistrate is merely formality.

Enquiry ought to have been conducted by Judicial Magistrate under the provisions under Section 173 (1) (a) of Cr.P.C.
9.
I have heard learned counsel for parties and perused the documents placed on record.

10. Undisputed facts which emerges from the submission made by learned counsel for parties as also the documents enclosed along with writ petition and reply is that on 26.05.2006 Manthirram Verma went to lodge report to the Police Station - Dongargarh.

He suffered head injuries in the police station, taken to hospital in the night by police and doctor in the postmortem report found that deceased suffered injury on scull, on right occipital area 3" above and lateral to the occipital protuberance.

CT scan report available on record mentions as under :-
"REPORT : Contiguous axial scan of 5mm thickness are taken from posterior fossa and 7 mm above it upto vertex.
 * Posterior fossa normal.
 * Supra Tentorial fossa  - Hypodense area with well defined geographical territory is visualized at Right frontal lobe on Right side lesion has CT values on 20 to 22HU.

5 - Hyperdense area visualised within core of lesion and at caudate nucleus and internal capsular region.
- Mass effect is visualised in the adjacent areas in the form of effacement of Right lateral ventricle and obliteration of C.S.F. spaces.

REMARKS : FINDINGS ARE SUGGESTIVE OF RIGHT M.C.A. CEREBRAL INFRACTION WITH HAEMORRHAGIC TRANSFORMATION.
ADVISED CLINICAL CORRELATION.

11. In view of above reports, I find it appropriate to deal with the enqury report submitted by Sub-Divisional Magistrate. Sub- Divisional Magistrate had recorded the statement and portion of their statement is also discussed in the enquiry report.

In the report, Sub-Divisional Magistrate,
considered the statement of police officials wherein they stated that illness/suffering of Manthirram Verma in the police station was not informed to Police Station Incharge (T.I.).

Smt. Indira Bai,
petitioner in her statement before Sub-Divisional Magistrate had narrated same fact as pleaded in the writ petition.
She stated that she has seen injures over the person of her husband late Manthirrvam Verma.
Station House Officer in his statement stated that Manthirram Verma was not taken into custody, he came to police station second time after consuming liquor for putting signature.
Dr. Suchita Shrivastava has not found any injuries on the body of late Manthirram Verma.
Constable Rekh Lal Bhalve in his statement stated that status of Manthirravm Verma in the police station was informed to Station House Officer (SHO) at that time he was in his residence.
The Station House Officer sent government jeep/vehicle on which Manthirram Verma was taken to hospital.
Head Constable, Jailal Sahu in his statement stated that when he was writing the report of Manthirram Verma he suddenly became ill, started shivering and fell down on the floor.
SHO came there and saw him and asked Mr. Thakur to take him to hospital.
This witness further stated that hand and legs of Manthirrvam Verma was not showing any movement.
Manthirram Verma want to urinate but he could not able to urinate.

Dr. Suchita Shrivastava, Medical Officer in her statement stated that when he was brought to the hospital, patient was making attempt to move due to which he was caught hold of by 1-2 person of his hands and legs and in attempt to turn, he fell down from the bed.
No external injury was seen by her.
12. Khusboo, S/o. Mohd. Gous, who was in the police station being arrested in the case of preventive action stated that he did not know Manthirram.
He did not see police officials assaulting anyone in the police station.
He was not inside the lockup room but he was sitting in handcuffs near the door.
One another man was sitting by his side he was not under handcuffs.
Police officials gave them food in the night at about 7.30 PM.

After taking the meals, police person asked him to get inside the lockup room, immediately thereafter his face tilted and fell down, at that time no other family members of that person were present in the police station.
Manthir Ram has not consumed liquor.
He also stated that said person was present before this witness was brought to the police station.

13. From perusal of the enquiry report as available on record submitted by Sub-Divisional Magistrate it is appearing that witnesses examined in their statement have made statement Smt. Indrabai vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37199428/
6 contradictory to each other.

sentences.text: Witness R.K. Tiwari, the then Station House Officer stated that Manthirram Verma was not taken into custody he was not arrested.
Whereas independent witnesses one of other accused present in the police station stated that Manthirram Verma was asked to go inside the lockup room.

One of the constable stated that Manthirram Verma came to police station in drunken conditions after consuming liquor, whereas independent witness stated that the other person, who was sitting by his side had not consumed liquor and he was present in the police station prior to his arrest i.e. prior to 5.00 PM.

Statement of this independent witness also falsify the story of police that Manthirram was sent back after initiating the proceedings under Section 155 of Cr.P.C.
and thereafter he again came to the police station at about 8.35 PM and he fell down while signing in the register.

Head Constable Rekhlal Bhalave who was on duty in the police station, stated that Manthirram along with two children came to the police station at about 11 to 11.30 AM for lodging report against Pitamber Verma.
His oral report was registered and he was sent for medical examination.
At 2.00 PM in the noon his duty was off and thereafter he again came in the night duty at about 21.30 and saw Manthirram lying on the floor, turned towards left side.
He was struggling and unable to talk.
Constable Jailal Sahu stated Manthirram suddenly became ill at the time of lodging of report.

Statement of this witness is contradictory to the statement of independent witness Khusboo son of Mohd.
Gous.
14. Independent witness has not stated about unrestness or struggling of Manthirram on the floor.
But the said fact was stated only by the police officials and Dr. Suchita Shrivastava.
Falling of patient from bed during treatment even when he was caught hold of by two persons by their hands and legs cannot be accepted without a pinch of salt.
Statement of doctor to this extent appears to be suspicious.

15. From the aforementioned facts of the case it is apparent that Manthirram who went to police station for lodging report is reported to be ill, however, in the postmortem report, liner fracture was found on the head which shows, death may be due to the injuries suffered by the deceased on his head in police station.

From considering the entire material available on record in particular the enquiry conducted by Sub- Divisional Magistrate and statement of witnesses, it is appearing that correct facts are not stated by the police person of police station, death of late Manthirram was on account of head injuries suffered by him, while he was in police station and his death was due to injuries suffered by him during his custody at police station.

16. The story narrated by the police appears to be concocted to this Court and in the opinion of this Court desperate attempt is made to avoid responsibility for the acts committed while Manthirram was in custody in police station.

17. In view of death of husband of petitioner due to the injuries suffered by deceased, in the police station, in the opinion of this Court petitioner is entitled for compensation under public law irrespective of the fact that petitioner had also remedy under civil law.

The claim in public law for compensation for unconstitutional deprivation of fundamental right to life and liberty, the protection of which is guaranteed under the Constitution, is a claim based on strict liability and is in addition to the claim available in private law for damages of tortious acts of the public servants.

19. Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Nilabati Behera (Smt.) Alias Lalita Behera Vs. State of Orissa and Others, reported in (1993) 2 SCC 746 in its majority view has observed that defence of sovereign immunity being inapplicable, and alien to the concept of guarantee of fundamental rights, there can be no question of such a defence being available in the constitutional remedy.

entities.text: Nilabati Behera (Smt.) Alias Lalita Behera Vs. State of Orissa and Others, reported in (1993) 2 SCC 746
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is this principle which justifies award of monetary compensation for contravention of fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution, when that is the only practicable mode of redress available for the contravention made by the State or its servants in the purported exercise of their powers, and enforcement of the fundamental right is claimed by resort to the remedy in public law under the Constitution by recourse to Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution.

This was enacted in case of Rudul Sah Vs. State of Bihar, reported in (1983) 4 SCC 141 and is basis of its subsequent decision in which compensation was awarded under Article 32 and 226 of the Constitution of India over contravention of fundamental rights.

20. Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of D.K. Basu Vs. State of W.B., reported in (1997) 1 SCC 416 has observed as under :-
"44.

entities.text: D.K. Basu Vs. State of W.B., reported in (1997) 1 SCC 416
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claim in public law for compensation for unconstitutional deprivation of fundamental right to life and liberty, the protection of which is guaranteed under the Constitution, is a claim based on strict liability and is in addition to the claim available in private law for damages of tortious acts of the public servants.
Public law proceedings serve a different purpose than the private law proceedings.

Award of compensation for established infringement of the indefeasible rights guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitutions is a remedy available in public law since the purpose of public law is not only to civilise public power but also to assure the citizens that they live under a legal system wherein their rights and interests shall be protected and preserved.

Grant of compensation in proceedings under Article 32 or 226 of the Constitution of India for the established violation or the fundamental rights guaranteed under Article 21, is an exercise of the Courts under the public law jurisdiction for penalising the wrongdoer and fixing the liability for the public wrong on the State which failed in the discharge of its public duty to protect the fundamental rights of the citizen.

45. The old doctrine of only relegating the aggrieved to the remedies available in civil law limits the role of the courts too much, as the protector and custodian of the indefeasible rights of the citizens.
The courts have the obligation to satisfy the social aspirations of the citizens because the court and the law are for the people and expected to respond to their aspirations.
A Court of law cannot close its consciousness and aliveness to stark realities.

Mere punishment of the offender cannot give much solace to the family of the victim - civil action for damage is a long Smt. Indrabai vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37199428/
8 drawn and cumber some judicial process.

sentences.text:
Monetary compensation for redressal by the Court finding the infringement of the indefeasible right to life of the citizen is,
therefore, useful and at times perhaps the only effective remedy to apply balm to the wounds of the family members of the deceased victim.
Who may have been the bread winner of the family."

21. So far as the submission of learned counsel for respondents No.5 to 11 that petitioner has also filed civil suit seeking compensation of Rs.10.00 Lakhs and therefore, relief of compensation as prayed for by petitioner in this petition cannot be granted is concerned, in the aforementioned judgment, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that order for payment of amount as compensation under public law is on the ground of unconstitutional depriving of fundamental right to life and liberty.

The remedy of civil law will not come on the way to provide appropriate amount of compensation if the Court comes to the conclusion that there is unconstitutional deprivation of fundamental rights as the Courts have obligation to satisfy the social aspirations of the citizens because the Court and the law are for the people and expected to respond to their aspirations.

The incident is of 26.05.2006 and writ petition is filed immediately thereafter on 26.10.2006.
22.

So far as the relief of punishing the responsible police officer and registering of criminal case against respondents is concerned, perusal of the documents placed before the Court it is appearing that complaint case is already filed before the Court of jurisdictional Magistrate and therefore, this Court is not considering that issue and leaving it open to be decided in that proceeding based on the evidence brought before it.
23.
For the forgoing discussions made here-in-above, I am inclined to allow this petition in part.

Accordingly, this petition is allowed in part and the respondents/State are directed to pay an amount of Rs.3.00 lakhs (Three Lakhs) as compensation to petitioner in lieu of death of her husband for the reasons as discussed above within a period of two months.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The death of petitioner was due to custodial torture and assault, in violation of human dignity.
Late Manthirram Verma was working as Supervisor at Bajrang Power Ispat Limited and earning Rs.5,000/- per month and petitioner has no other source of income, therefore, petitioner be awarded suitable amount of compensation and further a direction be issued to Central Bureau of Investigation for proper investigation into the matter.
The police personnel failed to give plausible explanation as to how Manthirram Verma suffered injuries when his children left Manthirram Verma in the evening in a good health condition.
Custodial death is one of the worst crime and is protected under Article 21 and 22 (1) of the Constitution of India.
He contended that as the incident is of police station, the report submitted by Sub-Divisional Magistrate also does not mention the correct conclusion.
From the report submitted it is clearly depicting that report is not prepared in fair manner.
Petitioner be awarded compensation, the respondent/CBI be directed to investigate the incident of death of late Manthirram Verma.
Thereafter, Pitambar lodged report at about 13.30 hours.
He suffered paralysis attack of his left part of the body and further he also fell down from bed in the hospital during treatment.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Falling of patient from bed during treatment even when he was caught hold of by two persons by their hands and legs cannot be accepted without a pinch of salt.
Statement of doctor to this extent appears to be suspicious.
15. From the aforementioned facts of the case it is apparent that Manthirram who went to police station for lodging report is reported to be ill, however, in the postmortem report, liner fracture was found on the head which shows, death may be due to the injuries suffered by the deceased on his head in police station.
From considering the entire material available on record in particular the enquiry conducted by Sub- Divisional Magistrate and statement of witnesses, it is appearing that correct facts are not stated by the police person of police station, death of late Manthirram was on account of head injuries suffered by him, while he was in police station and his death was due to injuries suffered by him during his custody at police station.
17. In view of death of husband of petitioner due to the injuries suffered by deceased, in the police station, in the opinion of this Court petitioner is entitled for compensation under public law irrespective of the fact that petitioner had also remedy under civil law.
Smt. Indrabai vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37199428/
7 18.
The claim in public law for compensation for unconstitutional deprivation of fundamental right to life and liberty, the protection of which is guaranteed under the Constitution, is a claim based on strict liability and is in addition to the claim available in private law for damages of tortious acts of the public servants.
19. Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Nilabati Behera (Smt.) Alias Lalita Behera Vs. State of Orissa and Others, reported in (1993) 2 SCC 746 in its majority view has observed that defence of sovereign immunity being inapplicable, and alien to the concept of guarantee of fundamental rights, there can be no question of such a defence being available in the constitutional remedy.
It is this principle which justifies award of monetary compensation for contravention of fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution, when that is the only practicable mode of redress available for the contravention made by the State or its servants in the purported exercise of their powers, and enforcement of the fundamental right is claimed by resort to the remedy in public law under the Constitution by recourse to Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution.
The remedy of civil law will not come on the way to provide appropriate amount of compensation if the Court comes to the conclusion that there is unconstitutional deprivation of fundamental rights as the Courts have obligation to satisfy the social aspirations of the citizens because the Court and the law are for the people and expected to respond to their aspirations.
So far as the relief of punishing the responsible police officer and registering of criminal case against respondents is concerned, perusal of the documents placed before the Court it is appearing that complaint case is already filed before the Court of jurisdictional Magistrate and therefore, this Court is not considering that issue and leaving it open to be decided in that proceeding based on the evidence brought before it.
